purpose: Compare a recurrent stateful neuron candidate with flat MLP controls on the same synthetic sequence-sum task.
hypothesis: Explicit state improves sequence-sum fit over a state-reset ablation; accuracy and efficiency depend on whether parameter or compute budget is matched.

task.name: sum_five_values
task.split: independent fixed seeds per run; no test split

stateful_candidate.state_policy: carry state across all 5 sequence positions

state_reset_ablation.state_policy: reset to None before each of the 5 positions

stopping: Exactly 250 optimizer steps per model; no tuning against validation results.
alignment: All models use identical training and validation examples, optimizer, step count, and batch size. Stateful candidate is compared separately against a near-equal parameter MLP and a near-equal forward-MAC MLP because those budgets cannot both be matched; the state-reset ablation matches candidate parameters and compute.
limitations: Synthetic train and validation data share one fixed sum rule; there is no held-out task or test split.
MAC counts include affine matrix products only, not bias, activations, optimizer, memory traffic, or framework overhead.
CPU latency is an observational microbenchmark and not a device-independent performance claim.
